- When sentiment is high (≥0.5) and forecast is significantly above true price, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is below true price, increase forecast by 5–10% to avoid underreaction.  
- After a sharp price spike (true > 70), model tends to overshoot; cap forecast at +10% above peak for next 3 days.  
- If true price drops below 65 after a spike, model often lags; adjust forecast to match true drop by day +1.  
- Mean reversion bias: if 3 consecutive days show forecast > true, reduce forecast by 2–3% per day until convergence.  
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., 0.8 → 0.2) triggers downward bias correction: reduce forecast by 5–8% for next 2 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true price when sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.27/0.80); add 2–3% to forecast if sentiment swings >0.3.
